paper.title: Near Inclusions of von Neumann Algebras, Without Small Spatial Embeddings
paper.html:
Abstract

We give a negative answer to the unrestricted small-spatial-embedding problem for one-sided near inclusions of von Neumann algebras. On separable complex Hilbert spaces, we construct pairs of unital von Neumann algebras with common identity whose one-sided gaps tend to zero. Spatial embeddings of the source into the target exist, but every implementing unitary stays a fixed positive distance from the identity. The obstruction therefore concerns small implementing unitaries, rather than the existence of spatial embeddings.

1 Introduction

Let M and N be von Neumann algebras acting on a complex Hilbert space H, both with identity IH​. Their one-sided near-inclusion gap is
γ(M,N)=x∈M∥x∥≤1​sup​y∈Ninf​∥x−y∥.(1.1)
The approximating element y is not required to be contractive. A small value of γ(M,N) says that every contraction in M is close to some element of N; it does not require these choices of approximants to preserve algebraic operations. If a unitary u satisfies uMu∗⊆N, then γ(M,N)≤2∥u−IH​∥. The converse question asks whether a small near inclusion can always be obtained in this way.
The underlying perturbation program began with Kadison and Kastler [8]. They measured the distance between operator algebras by the Hausdorff distance between their unit balls in the operator norm, now called the Kadison–Kastler distance, and proposed that sufficiently close von Neumann algebras should be related by a unitary close to the identity. Christensen, Johnson, and Raeburn–Taylor established the amenable case in the 1970s [2; 7; 10]. Christensen subsequently introduced near inclusions and proved a spatial embedding theorem for an amenable source algebra and an arbitrary target [3, Definition~2.1 and Theorem~4.3]. In particular, sufficiently small near inclusions in this setting admit implementing unitaries whose distance from the identity is bounded linearly by the near-inclusion tolerance.
We use the following formulation of the unrestricted one-sided question posed by Cameron, Christensen, Sinclair, Smith, White, and Wiggins in the paragraph preceding [1, Theorem~2]:
For every ε>0, is there a δ>0 such that, for every complex Hilbert space H and every pair of von Neumann algebras M,N⊆B(H) with common identity IH​, γ(M,N)<δ implies the existence of a unitary u∈B(H) satisfying
uMu∗⊆Nand∥u−IH​∥<ε?
Here δ must be independent of the algebras and their representations. We answer this question negatively.
Theorem 1.1.
There exist ε0​>0, separable complex Hilbert spaces Hn​, and von Neumann algebras Mn​,Nn​⊆B(Hn​) with common identity IHn​​ such that
γ(Mn​,Nn​)⟶0,
but, for all sufficiently large n, every unitary u∈B(Hn​) satisfying uMn​u∗⊆Nn​ obeys
∥u−IHn​​∥≥ε0​.
In these examples a unitary embedding of Mn​ into Nn​ does exist; the obstruction concerns its distance from the identity. The theorem therefore separates normwise approximation from small spatial implementation even on separable Hilbert spaces. Its hypothesis is one-sided. The construction supplies no reverse near inclusion, and hence does not give a counterexample to the two-sided Kadison–Kastler conjecture. The positive results for nonamenable factors in [1], which concern two-sided perturbations under additional structural hypotheses, address a different assertion.
The proof transfers a classical finite-dimensional obstruction into the near-inclusion problem. Voiculescu's clock and shift matrices Un​,Vn​∈B(Cn) satisfy ∥Un​Vn​−Vn​Un​∥→0, but cannot be approximated in norm by commuting unitary pairs [11]. Exel and Loring gave an elementary winding-number proof of this phenomenon [5]; we use its trace-logarithm form [4, Lemma~3.1]. We recall the short obstruction argument in Section 4.
To place these matrices in operator algebras, we use the free group F on countably many generators. The starting representation is the real-parameter Pytlik–Szwarc representation [9, \S2.3, Equation~(5)], whose cyclic coefficient is Haagerup's positive-definite function g↦t∣g∣, 0<t<1, where ∣g∣ is reduced word length [6, Lemma~1.2]. Section 2 gives a self-contained tree realization at t=1/2 and adds a circle parameter z. The norms of its Fourier coefficients are bounded, uniformly over the group, by a sequence with summable first moment. Along successive distinct free generators, the values of the representations converge in the weak operator topology to tz times the projection onto the identity vector in ℓ2(F). Substituting Un​ and Vn​ for the circle parameter therefore produces two unitary representations of F whose weak limits retain the original matrices.
Two further steps connect this representation family to the theorem. In Section 3, a diagonal unitary built from the two representations conjugates a copy of the group von Neumann algebra of F×F. The target Nn​ is the commutant of an amplified right regular representation of this product group. Reordering the Fourier expansions gives an approximant in Nn​ and an error bounded by a constant times ∥Un​Vn​−Vn​Un​∥. Crucially, this estimate holds on the entire unit ball of the source algebra. In Section 4, a hypothetical sequence of spatial embeddings tending to the identity places the conjugated left regular representation in Nn​, where it commutes with the right regular representation. Their pointwise product is then a representation of F×F, so the von Neumann algebras generated by its two factors commute. Weak operator limits in these algebras recover operators close to copies of Un​ and Vn​ supported on projections. Perturbing those projections, compressing to a common finite-dimensional corner, and taking polar parts would yield commuting unitary matrices close to Un​,Vn​, contradicting the winding-number obstruction.

4 Recovering the matrix obstruction

The preceding construction turns a small commutator into a small one-sided gap. We now show that a spatial embedding close to the identity would turn the original matrix pair into a nearby commuting pair. Choosing the clock and shift matrices will make this impossible.

4.1 The winding obstruction

The matrices below are Voiculescu's almost commuting unitary pair [11]. We include the logarithmic winding argument, in the form developed in [5; 4].
Lemma 4.1.
For n≥3, let Un​,Vn​ be the unitaries on Cn given by
Un​ej​=ωnj​ej​,Vn​ej​=ej+1modn​,ωn​=e2πi/n(0≤j<n).(4.1)
Then νn​:=∥Un​Vn​−Vn​Un​∥=∣ωn​−1∣→0. There is no infinite subsequence along which commuting unitaries Un​,Vn​ on Cn satisfy
∥Un​−Un​∥+∥Vn​−Vn​∥⟶0.
Proof.
The identity Un​Vn​=ωn​Vn​Un​ proves the first assertion. For any unitary matrices U,V whose commutator UVU∗V∗ has no eigenvalue −1, define
κ(U,V)=2πi1​Trlog(UVU∗V∗),
using the principal logarithm and the unnormalized trace. The determinant identity
exp(Trlog(UVU∗V∗))=det(UVU∗V∗)=1
shows that κ(U,V) is an integer. It is continuous, and hence constant, along any path on which the logarithm remains defined. For the pair in (4.1), its value is 1, since Un​Vn​Un∗​Vn∗​=ωn​I and 0<2π/n<π. For a commuting pair its value is 0.
Suppose the asserted approximants existed along a subsequence. For all sufficiently large n on that subsequence, write Un∗​Un​=eiAn​ and Vn∗​Vn​=eiBn​, with An​,Bn​ self-adjoint and spectra in (−π,π). The paths
Un​(s)=Un​eisAn​,Vn​(s)=Vn​eisBn​(0≤s≤1)
stay within the respective endpoint distances from Un​,Vn​. Indeed, for ∣θ∣<π and 0≤s≤1, ∣eisθ−1∣≤∣eiθ−1∣. A four-factor telescoping estimate gives, uniformly in s,
∥Un​(s)Vn​(s)Un​(s)∗Vn​(s)∗−I∥≤νn​+2∥Un​−Un​∥+2∥Vn​−Vn​∥⟶0.
The principal logarithm is therefore defined along the whole path for all sufficiently large n. Its integer changes from 1 to 0, a contradiction.
∎

4.2 A finite-dimensional corner

Compression of commuting operators to a prescribed subspace need not preserve commutation. The next lemma avoids this difficulty by replacing each support projection by a nearby projection in its corresponding algebra and then using their common range.
Lemma 4.2.
For each n, let E1n​,E2n​ be commuting projections on a complex Hilbert space Hn​, with Dn​=En​Hn​ nonzero and finite-dimensional, where En​=E1n​E2n​. Let R1n​,R2n​ be unitaries commuting with both projections, and write Rin​=Rin​∣Dn​​. Suppose A1n​,A2n​⊂B(Hn​) are commuting unital von Neumann algebras and there are Tin​∈Ain​ such that
∥Tin​−Ein​Rin​∥⟶0(i=1,2).(4.2)
Then, for all sufficiently large n, there are commuting unitaries R1n​,R2n​ on Dn​ with
∥Rin​−Rin​∥⟶0(i=1,2).
Proof.
We first replace the intended projections by nearby projections in the commuting algebras. Set δin​=∥Tin​−Ein​Rin​∥. Since (Ein​Rin​)∗(Ein​Rin​)=Ein​,
din​:=∥Tin∗​Tin​−Ein​∥≤δin​(2+δin​)⟶0.
For sufficiently large n, take the spectral projection
Qin​=1(1/2,∞)​(Tin∗​Tin​)∈Ain​.
The spectrum of Tin∗​Tin​ lies in [0,din​]∪[1−din​,1+din​]. This follows from the resolvent bound for a self-adjoint operator within din​ of a projection. Functional calculus therefore gives
∥Qin​−Tin∗​Tin​∥≤din​,∥Qin​−Ein​∥≤2din​⟶0.
Since the two algebras commute, Pn​=Q1n​Q2n​ is a projection, and
∥Pn​−En​∥≤∥Q1n​−E1n​∥+∥Q2n​−E2n​∥⟶0.
We identify this perturbed corner with Dn​ by a small unitary. The operator
Sn​=Pn​En​+(I−Pn​)(I−En​)=I+(Pn​−En​)(2En​−I)
tends to the identity in norm and satisfies Sn​En​=Pn​Sn​. It is invertible for large n. Its absolute value commutes with En​, so its unitary polar part Jn​=Sn​(Sn∗​Sn​)−1/2 satisfies
Jn​En​Jn∗​=Pn​,∥Jn​−I∥⟶0.(4.3)
In particular, Pn​Hn​ has exactly the dimension of Dn​.
The compressions Pn​T1n​Pn​ and Pn​T2n​Pn​ commute, including across adjoints. This needs a check because Qin​ need not commute with Tin​. Suppress n and put A=Q1​T1​Q1​∈A1​ and B=Q2​T2​Q2​∈A2​. The two compressions are AQ2​ and Q1​B. Since AQ1​=Q1​A=A, BQ2​=Q2​B=B, and every element of A1​ commutes with every element of A2​, both orders of their product equal AB. Replacing A or B by its adjoint proves the other commutations.
Transfer these compressions to Dn​ using (4.3):
Cin​=En​Jn∗​Tin​Jn​En​∣Dn​​.
The pair still commutes across adjoints. Moreover,
∥Cin​−Rin​∥≤δin​+2∥Jn​−I∥⟶0,
by comparing Tin​ with Ein​Rin​ before conjugation. Thus Cin​ is invertible for large n and ∥Cin∗​Cin​−IDn​​∥→0. Its unitary polar part
Rin​=Cin​(Cin∗​Cin​)−1/2
remains close to Rin​. The unital C∗-algebras generated by C1n​ and C2n​ commute; continuous functional calculus puts each polar part in its respective algebra. Hence the two polar unitaries commute, as required.
∎

4.3 Proof of the main theorem

Apply the construction of Section 3 to D=Cn and the clock–shift pair of Lemma 4.1. Use subscripts n for the resulting objects Ln​,Hn​,an​,bn​,fn​,Wn​,Mn​,Nn​. All these Hilbert spaces are separable. By Proposition 3.1,
γ(Mn​,Nn​)≤Cνn​⟶0.(4.4)
Proof of Theorem 1.1.
We show that no infinite subsequence admits unitaries un​ with
un​Mn​un∗​⊂Nn​,∥un​−I∥⟶0.(4.5)
Suppose otherwise and work on that subsequence. Define, for g∈G,
Zn​(g)=Wn​(λ(g)⊗ILn​​)Wn∗​,Σn​(g)=un​Zn​(g)un∗​(ρ(g)⊗ILn​​).
The first factor in the expression for Σn​(g) lies in Nn​, by (4.5). Thus the two representations being multiplied have commuting ranges, and Σn​ is a unitary representation of G. Proposition 3.1 gives the uniform estimate
g∈Gsup​​Σn​(g)−λ(g)ρ(g)⊗fn​(g)​≤βn​,βn​=Cνn​+2∥un​−I∥⟶0.(4.6)
Let A1n​ and A2n​ be the von Neumann algebras generated by the restrictions of Σn​ to F×{e} and {e}×F, respectively. These algebras commute.
We will apply Lemma 4.2 by taking weak limits of the generators in each factor. Under S=K⊗K, write
Hn​=K⊗K⊗K⊗K⊗Cn.
Let E1n​ use pe​ in the first and third slots, and let E2n​ use pe​ in the second and fourth slots, with identities in all other slots. These projections commute, and En​=E1n​E2n​ has range naturally identified with Cn. Let R1n​ and R2n​ act as Un​,Vn​, respectively, on the final slot and as the identity elsewhere.
Set g1j​=(sj​,e) and g2j​=(e,sj​). On the i-th factor of S, the operator λ(gij​)ρ(gij​) sends δx​ to δsj​xsj−1​​. For each fixed nonidentity word x, this conjugate leaves every finite subset of F as j→∞: for large j, the letter sj​ occurs neither in x nor in the finitely many words under consideration. Hence the conjugation operators converge weakly to pe​ in that slot. Combining this observation with (3.2) gives, for each fixed n and i,
λ(gij​)ρ(gij​)⊗fn​(gij​)WOTj→∞​tEin​Rin​.(4.7)
Here tensor products of bounded weakly convergent sequences on separate slots converge weakly, as follows first on elementary tensors and then by density. The finite spectral decompositions used in (3.2) justify the matrix-valued factor.
For each i,n, choose a weak operator cluster point Bin​ of Σn​(gij​) as j→∞. Such a point exists by weak operator compactness of the closed unit ball of B(Hn​), and belongs to Ain​. Norm balls are weak operator closed, so (4.6) and (4.7) imply
∥Bin​−tEin​Rin​∥≤βn​.
Thus Tin​=t−1Bin​∈Ain​ satisfies (4.2). No product of weak limits is used: commutation comes from membership in the two commuting algebras. Lemma 4.2 now produces commuting unitary matrices on Cn approaching Un​,Vn​ in norm. This contradicts Lemma 4.1, proving that (4.5) cannot hold on any infinite subsequence.
It follows that some ϵ0​>0 bounds ∥u−IHn​​∥ from below for every implementing unitary and all sufficiently large n. Otherwise one could choose increasing nj​ and implementing unitaries with distance less than 1/j, contrary to what we have just proved. Together with (4.4), this is Theorem 1.1.
∎
